safety_verdicts.content: Headache is still present at the time of consultation.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts do not explicitly state the headache is still present at the time of consultation.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Whether the headache is ongoing at the time of consultation affects acuity assessment and follow-up/safety-netting; an omission could understate persistence and severity. However, other context (woke patient, still symptomatic discussion) likely still drives appropriate management in most cases.

safety_verdicts.content: Paracetamol taken by the patient did not relieve the headache.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated notes paracetamol was taken but does not state it was ineffective.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Documenting lack of response to paracetamol informs treatment escalation (e.g., NSAID/triptan consideration) and can help differentiate headache types. Omission could lead to repeating an ineffective medication, but the plan already moved toward ibuprofen, limiting likely harm.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not mention living with a partner.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Living situation (with a partner) is useful for psychosocial context and safety-netting support, but omission rarely changes acute headache diagnosis or treatment. This is primarily a social history documentation gap.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not mention smoking status.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Smoking status contributes to vascular risk profiling but is not central to the immediate management of an otherwise uncomplicated headache presentation. Its omission is unlikely to cause direct clinical harm in this encounter.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Not in gold, and the transcript does not clearly contain an explicit patient denial of brain injury (question is asked but response is not captured).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Recording “no brain injury” without a clearly captured patient denial can falsely close off consideration of trauma-related intracranial pathology and may reduce appropriate questioning or safety-netting. While the overall scenario sounds non-traumatic, this incorrect negative history has meaningful potential to mislead future clinicians reviewing the note.
